Mujahid Ali Shah, PhD

Postdoctoral researcher, Department of Molecular Biology and Genetics, Aarhus University, Denmark

I study how the gut's nervous system and immune system work together, and how the intestine repairs itself after injury. My model is the zebrafish, whose transparent larvae let me watch it happen in a living animal.

See my research Publications

Research: how the gut repairs itself

The intestine is lined by a single sheet of epithelium, wired by its own nervous system and patrolled by immune cells. I use zebrafish, whose transparent larvae let me watch these systems in a living animal, to understand how they talk to each other in health and after injury.

Enteric nervous system

Regeneration of the gut's nervous system

How enteric neurons are lost and rebuilt, and how the regenerated network restores gut function.

Neuroimmune

Neuroimmune communication in the gut

How enteric neurons and immune cells interact, and how that crosstalk shapes intestinal health.

Repair

Intestinal injury and repair

How the intestinal lining responds to damage and inflammation, and what helps it recover.

Environment

Western-style diet and the microbiota

How a Western-style diet, and the microbes an animal carries, influence the gut's nerves, immunity and repair.

Approach

My work brings together neuroscience, immunology and microbiology in one whole-animal model.

  • ModelZebrafish (Danio rerio) larvae and adults, transgenic and reporter lines
  • ImagingLive and high-resolution fluorescence microscopy, including light-sheet imaging
  • Genetic toolsTargeted cell ablation and regeneration models
  • MolecularMolecular biology and transcriptomics
  • PhysiologyGut function and behavioural assays
